title.narrative: Managing Exits from Armed Conflicts (MEAC) Project

description.narrative:
UNIDIR’s Managing Exits from Armed Conflict (MEAC) is a multi-year, collaborative “One UN” project run in partnership with IOM, DPO, UNDP, UNICEF, and the World Bank. Through large-scale, longitudinal, multi-method country-specific studies MEAC has been supporting practitioners and policymakers with its first-of-its-kind data and analyses to inform more effective prevention and reintegration interventions since 2020.
The MEAC-project examines the trajectories of girls, boys, women, and men exiting armed groups and returning to civilian life. MEAC seeks to understand the factors that drive recruitment into armed groups and those that bolster transitions to civilian life in order to inform evidence-based policy and practice to prevent and resolve armed conflict and build peace. MEAC’s data and analysis advance the design of interventions along the humanitarian, peace, and development nexus, from DDR to IDP reintegration and inclusive peace processes. In collaboration with local research partners on the ground, MEAC operates multi-method, longitudinal case studies in six countries – Nigeria, Chad, Niger, Cameroon, Colombia, and Iraq – and shares its actionable evidence with local practitioners, donors, and UN partners to inform policy and practice.
As a result of its work, MEAC is generating some of the largest data sets on conflict exits and reintegration processes around the world and has produced unique insights on the factors that led to recruitment and association in the first place. Backed by a stronger evidence base on the factors that facilitate full and sustainable exits from conflict, the international community will be better able to craft cross-sectoral interventions to effectively interrupt conflict cycles, foster reconciliation, and build lasting peace.
